wy_box_canyon_central.blurb: Box Canyon (Central) is a bouldering zone in the Vedauwoo rocks, in the Laramie range of southeast Wyoming. The problems sit on the side walls of the canyon, close to the paved footpaths, so the walk between boulders is short. The stone is granite. Roughly ten problems are known: about half are easy to moderate, V1 to V3, with a small group of much harder lines from V6 up to V8 for strong climbers. A couple of the lines follow cracks, which suits the crack-heavy character of the wider Vedauwoo area. It makes a handy stop for a quick session or a warm-up before heading to the roped climbing nearby.

wy_cove_the.blurb: The Cove is a small sport-climbing wall in Vedauwoo, near Laramie, Wyoming, tucked into a granite overhang on the hillside above and opposite the Beehive Buttress. It holds around ten bolted routes, mostly in the 5.10 to 5.12 range: a few at 5.10, the bulk at 5.11, and a couple at the low end of 5.12. This is a good pick for climbers who want steep, pumpy face climbing rather than the cracks Vedauwoo is famous for. The cove tends to be shaded in the morning and catches sun later in the day, making it a comfortable summer choice. It is not a beginner crag.

wy_lower_blair_ii.blurb: Lower Blair II is the middle of three neighbouring rock masses in the Lower Blair group, in the Vedauwoo region near Laramie, Wyoming, at around 8,000 feet. It holds about ten climbs, almost all of them trad with a single sport line, and the granite offers mostly cracks. Grades run from 5.8 up to low 5.12, though the majority fall around 5.11, so it suits climbers comfortable on harder gear routes. The setting is forested, shady and quiet, with far fewer visitors than the main Vedauwoo formations, and it is easy to find your way around compared with the bigger Upper Blair.

wy_3_best_god_in_show_area.blurb: Best God in Show Area is the third zone of Fairfield Central on Fairfield Hill, above Sinks Canyon near Lander, Wyoming. It has ten bolted sport routes on a tall, clean wall of dolomite that shows rippled, vertical climbing with a steeper bulge and loose roof overhead; only a couple of lines tackle the steepest ground. Grades start at 5.10 with two easier routes, add two at 5.11, and the majority, six of ten, are 5.12, so it is best for climbers already leading hard. The wall sits in a sheltered nook, and the hill around it is known for being sunny on cold days.

wy_owl_roofs.blurb: Owl Roofs is a small bouldering spot on the north side of Rawlins, Wyoming, just beyond the old prison. The rock is good quartzite shaped into two main roofs; the western one is bigger and has more features, and the best long traverse-out line starts there. Around ten problems are known. Most are mid-grade, with six at V3 and a couple more in the V3 to V4 range, plus a few much harder projects up to V9 for the strong. It is not worth a special trip, but it gives about an hour of enjoyable bouldering if you are passing along I-80. A pad is handy at the lip.

wy_cutfinger_rock.blurb: Cutfinger Rock is one of three historic boulders beside the path near Jenny Lake in Grand Teton National Park, Wyoming, at about 6,800 feet. It is a short walk from the campground and ranger station area, and the south face is the first one you meet on the left of the path. Ten problems are known, spanning a wide range: a handful of easy lines from VB to V1, a couple of mid-grade problems around V5, and a few hard ones reaching V9 and V10. Easy mantles and bulges make it a decent spot for newer boulderers, while the steeper lines give experienced climbers something to try.

wy_coolsville.blurb: Coolsville is a sport-climbing sector in the Downtown group of crags in Ten Sleep Canyon, in the Bighorn Mountains of north-central Wyoming. The trail from the roadside parking climbs in zigzags to reach the wall. It has around ten bolted routes with a middle-to-hard grade spread: two at 5.10, three at 5.11, four at 5.12 and one 5.13. A central buttress carrying several 5.12 lines defines the sector, so it is a good objective for climbers working the harder grades, while those looking for easier mileage will want to head to other walls in the canyon.

wy_2_claim_jumper.blurb: Claim Jumper is a sport-climbing section of the central cliff at Wild Iris, on the plateau above Lander, Wyoming, at roughly 8,900 feet. About ten bolted routes are known, and the grades give it a wider spread than most walls in the area: a few easy lines from 5.5 to 5.9, then two at 5.10 and three at 5.11. Holds are described as bigger than on many easy slabs, which makes it a friendly place for beginners and climbers building up to harder routes. Nearby sections of the same cliff are home to mostly 5.10 and 5.11 climbing, so a mixed group can split up and still stay close together.
